title: The Induction Lamp - Types and Inventors
description: The Induction Lamp creates a discharge in a tube or bulb without having electrodes inside the vessel. It uses electromagnetic fields to excite a filling. There are two kinds of fluorescent induction lamps: internal and external. Johann Hittorf first developed the lamp in 1884. Nikola Tesla created his own version. P.C. Hewitt made mercury vapor induction lamps, and John M. Anderson (GE) invented the modern consumer induction lamp in 1967 in Schenectady, New York. Philips sold the first lamp in the QL series after the GE patent expired.
author: Edison Tech Center
